newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds remain in shadow of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds remain in shadow of FOMC.

text.p: *Australian bonds saw an extremely thin session as the market remained in the shadow of Tuesday's FOMC meeting where a tightening in policy is seen as a strong possibility.
Australian bonds saw an extremely thin session as the market remained in the shadow of Tuesday's FOMC meeting where a tightening in policy is seen as a strong possibility, traders said.
Local yields were marginally lower after treading a narrow range, but turnover was restricted to just over 3,000 lots when a normal day would see over 10,000.

A 25 basis point U.S. rate hike has largely been factored in, but such a move, the first tightening in some 1-1/2 years, would likely have an initial negative reaction in U.S. Treasuries and spill over to debt markets globally.
However, if the increase in rates is cited as a pro-active move to stem a potential blow-out in U.S. inflation, the sell-off could prove short-lived, analysts said.

The local market is seen weathering any fall-out in the U.S. market reasonably well, given Australia's current positive outlook on inflation and with a further easing in policy seen possible before then end of the year.

But "I think the long bonds here can't rally much further unless the writing's on the wall for another rate cut," said Stephen Koukoulas, senior economist at Citibank Australia. He saw the 10-year bond yields at 7.50 percent on an easing.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread narrowed slightly to resistance at 110 basis points as the local market established a modest firm tone. Last week, this spread briefly dipped to 106 basis points. However, there was no trade in U.S. Treasuries in Asian time due to a holiday in Japan.
